responsibility: Implementation of the ObjC++ declaration-adaptation layer that lets Objective-C parsing/actions reuse C++ front-end machinery with Objective-C semantics where needed. It wraps C++ routines for starting and finishing struct definitions, cross-referencing tags, comparing types, beginning and ending compound statements, and finalizing functions, managing details such as pushing an extern-"C" language context for Objective-C ivar/record layout, inserting fields through C++ member-declaration paths, checking duplicate Objective-C ivars, and explicitly calling `expand_or_defer_fn` after `finish_function` so ObjC++ function bodies are lowered the way the C++ front end expects.
same_name_distinction: Implementation source for the ObjC++ declaration remapping layer declared in objcp-decl.h: it defines the objcp_* wrappers that perform the runtime bridging to C++ front-end behavior, such as pushing/popping an extern-"C" context around struct handling, feeding fields through C++ member-declaration paths, checking duplicate Objective-C ivars, and forcing RTL generation after finish_function. Unlike the header twin, it provides executable wrapper logic rather than macro-based name redirection and declarations.
